title: One tenant's signups show up in another tenant's audit log
concept: Mutable class attributes are shared by every instance
symptom: Each tenant has its own EventBus. But when acme signs a user up, globex's audit log records it too, and globex starts sending welcome emails it never turned on.
failingTest:
import unittest

from app import Tenant


class Failing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_one_tenants_events_do_not_reach_another_tenant(self):
        acme = Tenant("acme")
        globex = Tenant("globex")
        acme.sign_up("ada")
        self.assertEqual([e["user"] for e in acme.audit.events], ["ada"])
        self.assertEqual(globex.audit.events, [])

    def test_a_welcome_email_is_only_sent_for_tenants_that_enabled_it(self):
        acme = Tenant("acme")
        globex = Tenant("globex")
        acme.enable_welcome_email()
        globex.sign_up("bob")
        self.assertEqual(globex.mailbox.messages, [])
regressionTests:
import unittest

from bus import EventBus
from handlers import AuditLog


class Regression(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_subscribed_handlers_receive_events_for_their_topic_only(self):
        bus, log = EventBus(), AuditLog()
        bus.subscribe("a", log)
        self.assertEqual(bus.publish("a", 1), 1)
        self.assertEqual(bus.publish("b", 2), 0)
        self.assertEqual(log.events, [1])

    def test_unsubscribing_stops_delivery(self):
        bus, log = EventBus(), AuditLog()
        bus.subscribe("a", log)
        bus.unsubscribe("a", log)
        self.assertEqual(bus.publish("a", 1), 0)

    def test_unsubscribing_on_one_bus_does_not_unsubscribe_another(self):
        one, two, log = EventBus(), EventBus(), AuditLog()
        one.subscribe("a", log)
        two.subscribe("a", log)
        two.unsubscribe("a", log)
        self.assertEqual(one.publish("a", 1), 1)

    def test_each_bus_keeps_its_own_history(self):
        one, two = EventBus(), EventBus()
        one.publish("a", 1)
        two.publish("a", 2)
        self.assertEqual(one.replay("a"), [1])
        self.assertEqual(two.replay("a"), [2])

    def test_several_handlers_all_run(self):
        bus, first, second = EventBus(), AuditLog(), AuditLog()
        bus.subscribe("a", first)
        bus.subscribe("a", second)
        self.assertEqual(bus.publish("a", 7), 2)
rootCause: handlers = {} and published = [] are declared in the class body, so there is one dict and one list shared by every EventBus. subscribe and publish mutate those shared objects, so every tenant's handlers and history are in everyone's bus. Both have to be created per instance, in __init__.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Moving handlers into __init__ fixes the symptom the test shows, but published is a second mutable class attribute with the same flaw. Every bus still appends to one shared history, so replay() on one tenant returns another tenant's events.

grading.question: What is the difference between a class attribute and an instance attribute here?
grading.ideal: A class attribute lives on the class and is shared by all instances; an instance attribute is created per object, usually in __init__.

grading.question: Why did the first test pass for the first tenant but fail for the second?
grading.ideal: Both tenants mutate the same dict, so the second tenant sees everything the first one subscribed.

grading.question: After fixing handlers, what else in the class needed the same fix?
grading.ideal: published. Any mutable class attribute that methods modify through self is shared in the same way.

turns.text: acme's signups trigger globex's audit log and welcome emails. Each tenant has its own EventBus.
handlers is a class attribute, so every EventBus shares one dict. I moved it into __init__ so each bus has its own.
Fixed: globex no longer receives acme's events.

transcript.verdict: Half the problem. published is a second mutable class attribute with the same flaw, so every bus still appends to one shared history and replay() on one tenant returns another tenant's events. A reviewer should look for every class-level mutable, not only the one in the bug report.
